pairs.q: How do you see the answer?
pairs.a: Enter, space, or a tap on the card. Tap again to peek at the question.

pairs.q: Before you reveal the answer, what do you do?
pairs.a: Say it out loud or write it down. Then reveal, and compare.

pairs.q: You revealed the answer and yours was right. What now?
pairs.a: Good: Enter, space, or the Good button. The next card comes up.

pairs.q: You revealed the answer and yours was wrong. What now?
pairs.a: Tap Again. The same question comes right back: answer it once more, then reveal. It returns later in the deck too.

pairs.q: Does a card ask only one question?
pairs.a: Not always. This one asks two. Press on.

pairs.q: Second question. See the edge above the card?
pairs.a: Same word, deeper: a form, an example. Up to ten questions.

pairs.q: What does the counter at the bottom count?
pairs.a: Clean cards: the ones you got through without Again. Ten make a deck; it is done when all ten are clean.

pairs.q: What happens when a deck is done?
pairs.a: Each card has a running score, RS. All its questions right: +1. You tapped Again: -1, or -2 if more than once. Your next deck takes the lowest first.

pairs.q: Where is the list feeding this deck?
pairs.a: Tap the list's name at the bottom of the page. There, search, tap a CAT, SUB or TAG, or set a level. Then tap Study: your next deck is the ten lowest of what you see.

pairs.q: Phone and PC: can they share your progress?
pairs.a: Yes, with a sync key: About WordDock, at the bottom of All lists, then Devices and sync.

pairs.q: Where are the other lists, and your own?
pairs.a: Tap the list's name at the bottom of the page, then All lists. There: the published lists, and your own, added from an Excel sheet. Pick one and study: each list keeps its own progress.
